title: Weak point Wednesday: Neck
summary: NH argues a thick neck, ideally as wide as the jaw, is the top aesthetic upgrade and protects against concussions and crash injuries. Pulls grow it initially, then isolation is needed: plate or band neck curls, extensions and side flexion in higher reps, good alignment and a shortened range on prone work. Avoid low-rep maxes and fighter bridges.
claims: A big neck is the number one thing to build for facial aesthetics; aim for the neck line to be parallel to the jaw line
Photoshopping a thick neck into a pencil neck immediately makes a face look worse with no other change; even non-lifters should train it
Long necks look dorky; thickening the neck makes it appear shorter, so long-necked men must train it
Pulls grow the neck at first because the traps stabilize and pull on it, but growth stalls and then isolation is needed
Start isolation early to learn the patterns, but neck and calves are the easiest areas to catch up on later
The neck responds very fast to flexion and extension; start with a 5 lb plate for curls, extensions and side work
Once neck growth stalls, train it 3x/week varying volume and intensity, possibly adding bands
My neck was 16 inches before any neck work, genetic, since I had a big neck at 16-18 without deadlifting
A thick neck can be the difference between life and death in a car crash and reduces concussion risk in contact sports
Training the neck may help the traps grow by developing the surrounding area
Bands work surprisingly well; plates become impractical near 45 lb; use a neck machine or a harness
Use high volume for the neck and never do 3-rep maxes: cervical disc injury can cause numbness and affect the whole spine
The neck recovers fast and tolerates a lot of volume; it should not cause pain
Train the neck with chin tucked and spine stacked; vary weights and reps per direction because strength differs
Beginners can train neck once or twice a week; some people train it daily
On prone neck work keep the bench close to the chin to cut the range; going lower makes the thoracic spine round and risks injury
Neck bridges are for fighters; bodybuilders just need curls
exercises: prone; bench close to chin to limit range
for fighters, not needed for bodybuilders
